summary: When child workflow start fails or is cancelled, the corresponding childWorkflowComplete map entry is not removed, creating an orphaned entry that leaks memory for the duration of workflow execution.
userImpact: Long-running workflows that repeatedly fail to start child workflows will gradually accumulate orphaned completion entries, leading to memory leaks over time.
rootCause: When child workflow start fails or is cancelled, the corresponding completion handler entry is not removed from the childWorkflowComplete map, causing it to never be garbage collected.
proposedFix: Delete the corresponding childWorkflowComplete entry in resolveChildWorkflowExecutionStart when the activation is failed or cancelled.
keyQuote: Since the child workflow never started, it will never complete, so this entry is orphaned and constitutes a memory leak for the duration of the workflow execution.
